## Limitations of this analysis

[P1]
P1.1 This comparison assumes the packages are released together; it does not hold for libraries that ship on their own schedule.
P1.2 However, the caching argument only applies if the CI runners keep a shared cache, which ours do not today.

content.markdown: This analysis is valid only if packages are released simultaneously, not if they have independent release schedules.
The caching benefits discussed are contingent on CI runners having a shared cache, which is not currently implemented.

This section outlines two key assumptions and limitations that impact the validity of the preceding analysis. The absence of a shared CI cache significantly reduces the applicability of any caching arguments.

metadata.takeaway: Analysis is limited by package release schedules and current CI caching capabilities.

content.markdown: This analysis assumes packages are released simultaneously; it's not applicable to libraries with independent release schedules.
